title: What is Node.js?
summary: Run a JavaScript file with Node.js and read command-line arguments from process.argv.

options: A new programming language that replaces JavaScript
A program that runs JavaScript outside the browser
quiz.explain: Node.js is a **runtime**: a program that can run JavaScript on your computer, without a browser. The language is still JavaScript.

quiz.q: Complete the command that runs the file app.js with Node.js.
quiz.explain: Type `node` followed by the file name in a terminal. Node reads the file and runs it from top to bottom.

quiz.q: You run `node show.js red blue`. What does this program print?
quiz.explain: `process.argv[0]` is the path of Node itself and `process.argv[1]` is the path of your file. Your own arguments start at index 2, so index 2 is `red`.

quiz.q: Which of these exists in the browser but NOT in Node.js?
quiz.explain: `document` belongs to the web page, so Node has no page to work with. Node adds its own tools instead, such as reading files and starting servers.

exercise.task:
In `greet.js`, print a greeting for the name given on the command line.

- If you run `node greet.js Asha`, print `Hello, Asha!`.
- If no name is given, print `Hello, stranger!`.
- Print exactly one line.
hints: The words typed after the file name are stored in `process.argv`. Your own arguments start at index 2.
Read `process.argv[2]`. If nobody typed a name, it is `undefined`, so you can use `||` to pick a default value.
